messages:
emma: FYI prod-us-west2 showing a warm-pool islanding effect: several nodes report fractional free GPUs but tiny pods remain Pending. Started ~20m ago.
rishi: grafana link? which panels?
emma: cluster/allocations -> gpu_pending_count up to 68, warmpool.util=12% in that rack. node/gpu_free_fraction shows 0.25-0.5 free on 4 nodes but scheduler isn't packing.
carla: did the rack-shadow taint roll finish last night? that agent added `gpu:rack-shadow=true:NoSchedule` to a subset of nodes to isolate training racks.
tom: yeah, the agent finished a full-extent rollout at 03:30 UTC. I saw a small mismatch in the scoping rules but thought it was fine.
emma: snippet from kubectl (trimmed):
```
# kubectl get pods -n prod | grep Pending
mini-recap-01       Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate
rerank-small-77     Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient gpu
```
rishi: autoscaler attempted scale-up at 1819999980, cloud returned OK for capacity but then spot supply failed for two attempts. No hard quota issues reported.
infra-bot: ALERT: [gpu-pending-pods] cluster-prod-us-west2 threshold breached (count=68) at 1819999975
carla: I dug into scheduler logs: affinity plugin treats `rack-shadow` as a hard NoSchedule taint during packing decisions even for `workloadClass=tiny`. That prevents fractional coalescing since those nodes are now off-limits.
tom: ouch. that matches my suspicion about scoping. The taint should've been applied only to nodes labeled `workload_bucket=training`, but agent used a label selector that matched more nodes.
emma: short-term mitigation options?
rishi: 1) patch tiny deployments with toleration for `gpu:rack-shadow` (fast) 2) flip scheduler to allow per-class fractional coalesce (tiny only) 3) temporarily revert the taint on the affected nodes.
carla: toleration patch example I used on a canary: 
```
kubectl patch deploy mini-recap -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"gpu:rack-shadow","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]'
```
ops-bot: Patch applied to mini-recap by emma at 1820000010.
emma: applied tolerations to 15% of tiny replicas as test; pending dropped from 68 -> 18 in ~6m. Warmpool util climbed to 54%. Cost delta small but visible.
rishi: note risk: mixing tiny inference into previously isolated racks could affect training bandwidth under load if a training job bursts. Monitor nvlink metrics.
tom: rolled a quick fix to the node-label agent to tighten selector; new agent image queued for canary (5% nodes) and added rollback hooks. PR #4521.
carla: long-term actions (infra-scheduler backlog): - make rack-shadow a soft preference for `workloadClass=tiny` - add per-workload coalescing whitelist in scheduler - add rollout gate: block taint/label agent if pending_gpus > 10 for 15m - reduce node lease TTL to 1m to speed rebalance - add simulated packing step in CI for label/taint changes.
emma: I'll open INFRA-2099 and add runbook steps: (1) patch tolerations, (2) scale provisioner if quota allows, (3) revert taint agent.
infra-bot: Incident INFRA-2099 created by emma at 1820000040.
rishi: follow-up: add a preflight quota & spot-supply check to rollout job so we don't assume capacity when moving isolation labels. Also add a canary metric check: if pending_gpus delta > 8 in 20m, abort.
tom: ack. PR will include the canary gating. I'll also add a scheduler unit test to ensure `workloadClass=tiny` bypasses rack-shadow for fractional packing.
ops-bot: Provisioner scale attempt by emma at 1820000065 returned InsufficientSpotCapacity. Logged to CLOUD-9407.
emma: current status at 1820000151: pending=12, warm-pool util=48%. Leaving alert on but removed paging. Will update INFRA-2099 with timeline and cost notes.
carla: thanks everyone 44d — we'll coordinate the tight selector deploy and schedule the postmortem next ops sync.
